- **Animal-powered machines (horse gin, treadwheel)** [`animal_power_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/animal_power_gin.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: memory and drawings of Brunelleschi's ox-hoist at the Duomo.
- **Water wheel** [`water_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_wheel.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Arno mills power grain milling and fulling. Other Tuscan streams drive paper mills and ironworks. Wheel performance depends on water supply, head and design. Local: Arno mills and weirs; Arte della Lana fulling mills.
- **Windmill** [`windmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Windmills are known on the Tuscan coast. River-powered milling is more familiar inland. Coastal millers offer a starting point for a wind-driven project. Elsewhere: Flanders and Holland; Castile; Aegean islands.
- **Water turbine** [`water_turbine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_turbine.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Hill mills use a horizontal wheel (ritrecine) struck by a jet, a crude turbine. Curved guide vanes and a closed casing are unknown. Local: millwrights of the Apennine valleys.
- **Crank, connecting rod and flywheel** [`crank_connecting_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crank_connecting_rod.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Cranks turn grindstones and braces; engineers draw crank-and-rod pumps and saws with flywheels, but few are built. Local: Francesco di Giorgio Martini (Siena); carpenters.
- **Piston pumps (suction and force pump)** [`piston_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/piston_pump.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Sienese engineers have drawn suction and force pumps since Taccola. Barrels are bored logs or cast bronze with leather valves; mines still mostly bail. Local: Francesco di Giorgio Martini (Siena); bronze founders; fountain masters.
- **Hydraulic ram** [`hydraulic_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_ram.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Needs a strong lead or bronze pipe, two valves and an air vessel; pipes burst if the air cushion is forgotten. Local: fountain masters; plumbers (lead pipe); bronze founders.
- **Charcoal burning** [`charcoal_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charcoal_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Charcoal burners supply every forge and furnace; fuel is the limit on all metalwork. Local: charcoal burners of the Casentino and Mugello; Casentino and Apennine forests; Maremma woods.
- **Deep coal mining (drainage, ventilation, safety lamp)** [`coal_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coal_mining.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. Tuscany has wood and only poor lignite; burning stones are known from travellers' reports and distrusted for their smoke. Elsewhere: Liege; Newcastle and London.
- **Coal gas lighting** [`gas_lighting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_lighting.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium
- **Argand lamp (hollow wick and glass chimney)** [`argand_lamp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/argand_lamp.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Olive-oil lamps with a solid wick are universal. Needs a woven tubular wick, a brass burner and a thin glass chimney that survives the heat. Local: Murano glassmakers; brass workers.
- **Drilling for brine, gas and oil** [`oil_drilling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oil_drilling.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Rock oil skimmed from seeps in the Apennines near Modena is sold as medicine. Wells are dug, not drilled; salt comes from the sea and Volterra's springs. Local: Volterra salt works. Elsewhere: Sichuan (China), percussion-drilled brine and gas wells; Montegibbio near Modena, oil seeps.
- **Steam reaction toy (aeolipile)** [`steam_aeolipile`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steam_aeolipile.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept medium. Hero's Pneumatica circulates in Greek manuscripts, with no printed Latin version. Vitruvius describes bronze aeolipiles blowing steam as a model of wind. Local: humanists of the Medici circle; Leonardo da Vinci (in Milan).
- **Boilers and the safety valve** [`safety_valve_boiler`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/safety_valve_boiler.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Coppersmiths make stills and cauldrons. A vessel and relief valve that withstand repeated pressurisation present unfamiliar problems of sealing and reliability. Local: coppersmiths; bronze founders.
- **Pistonless steam pump (Savery)** [`savery_steam_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/savery_steam_pump.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Soldered copper vessels and pipes are makeable but seams fail under steam; lift is limited and fuel use enormous.
